title: Demon Lord Beast
text: “Have a nice patrol~”

And so off I went, patrolling and keeping watch around Father’s house. Chasing off any suspicious characters was my job, I say. Big Sister and the Raph-species were already on guard duty, but this was just an extra precaution. Apparently Father’s sleep grows shallow whenever a pig or a woman gets too close. Sleeping alongside the Raph-species, though, lets him rest peacefully, or so I’ve heard. Incidentally, this was also Filo-tan’s house, but she was staying over at Fiancée’s place tonight.
“Raph.”
“Raph.”

The Raph-species were settling in for the night all around Father’s house, each in their own preferred spot. Since there was no problem with me, they let me pass through without fuss. How was Father doing, I wondered? It seemed that tonight Father wasn’t crafting accessories, mixing potions, or studying alchemy—he was simply sleeping.
“Ugh…”

I could hear Father talking in his sleep. He sounded a little pained. Peeking gently through a gap in the curtains, I saw Big Sister watching over sleeping Father. When she stroked his cheek, his mumbling grew quieter. For some reason it reminded me of Father comforting a young Big Sister once upon a time. Funny how the roles had reversed.
“Raph.”

Raph-chan was also stroking Father worriedly. Was he having a bad dream, perhaps? If I lingered too long peeking in, Big Sister and the others were bound to glare at me, so I decided to withdraw unless they called for help. And so I quietly slipped away.
The next morning. A sleepy-looking Father was going about his morning duties.
“Fwaaah…”
“You look sleepy, Father.”
I called out to him as he tended to the Raph-species in the monster barn.
“Ah, Motoyasu… Lately even when I sleep, I keep dreaming about work back in the village. Raphtalia and the others say I’ve been groaning in my sleep.”
“Is that so? Then shall I join you as well, so that Father may rest peacefully?”
“Don’t. It’s annoying enough without you adding to the chaos. Go play with the Filolials.”

Since Father had spoken thus, I devoted myself entirely to caring for Filolial-sama. Incidentally, Father had firmly instructed Tiger Girl—who was genuinely sleepy—to stay quiet at Tiger Guy’s house. During the day, everyone in the village had witnessed Father dozing off at the village meeting hall. Then, in the early afternoon, having finished his nap, Father was once again in the barn full of Raph-species, tending to Filolial-sama and the young Raph-species children. I, too, was busy attending to Filolial-sama.
“Raph!”
“Tally!”
“Ria!”
The other Raph-species lined up, waiting their turn to be brushed by Father. Big Sister was there too, though her expression was rather complicated.
“You seem to be having fun, Naofumi-kun.”
Just then, Arc arrived, accompanied by Ho-kun.
“I suppose.”
“Did you make these monsters yourself?”
“Yeah… something wrong with that?”
“Raph.”
Father answered while stroking a Raph-species and one of Filolial-sama’s young. Considering Arc and his companions were slayers of gods, I wondered if there was something forbidden about this.
“Nothing wrong at all. We haven’t designated the creation of life as taboo.”

“Yeah. Well, if you were forcing weird restrictions on the life you create and getting off on watching it suffer while struggling against them, that’d be a different story—but the stability of the little ones here is solid, and the spirits approve of them too.”
Arc and Ho-kun each offered their views.
“I see.”
“Raph!”
Raph-chan spread both arms toward Arc, demanding to be picked up. Arc smiled and lifted her, and Raph-chan promptly climbed right up onto his shoulder. A familiar sight, indeed.
“Fufu.”

Arc gazed fondly at the sight of Raph-chan there. Come to think of it, there had been a time when Keel, Luna-chan, and Arc were playing together. Luna-chan, in her chick form, had done something similar—perching on Arc’s shoulder or landing atop Keel’s head.
“…Personally, I sort of feel like it would’ve been fine if it were forbidden,” Big Sister muttered under her breath, but Father and Arc seemed to let it pass unnoticed.
“Ah, could this be jealousy~? You’re practically the same, so why not just have Naofumi-kun groom you too~?”
Ho-kun teased, whistling. I whistled along in imitation from a distance. Whooo, whooo.
“Please stop that. And don’t you dare do the same thing from over there, Spear Hero. It’s annoying.”
“Two birds of a feather from the same world.”
“Raph!”
Raph-chan whistled at Big Sister right along with him. Truly, Father ought to brush her as well, without question.
“I too would love for Father to comb my hair. Swish, swoosh! I say.”
“Motoyasu, don’t say creepy things too.”
“Fufufu, Motoyasu-kun. Don’t mind me—go ahead and bother Naofumi-kun instead.”
“Worry not, Ho-kun. I’d be delighted to groom you as well.”
“No, I quite genuinely don’t want that.”
While I was pestering them like this, Arc cradled Raph-chan and stroked her tail.
“This brings back memories—back when I first came to this world. This world, you see, was one where a friend of mine decided to settle down permanently.”
“Is that so? Was he a god slayer too?”
“Nope. Not at all. Just someone I looked after, through a bit of a connection. A boy with a big, fluffy tail. He had quite the complex about that tail of his.”
“Raph?”
Arc glanced at Raph-chan’s tail as he spoke.

“Well, he was born under rather special circumstances. That tail of his had the ability to absorb magic—it could even drain the mana right out of anyone who touched it. In the world he was born into, he was feared as a ‘Demon Lord Beast,’ but at heart, he was actually quite delicate.”
“That’s an ominous name.”
“Not as scary as the name suggests. I could touch it just fine, and we got along well.”
“A fluffy tail that drains magic, huh…”
“Something like the Absorb skill I can use, perhaps?”
Arc thought it over for a moment at my question, then nodded.
“Yeah. Except his activated on its own without him even trying—more like that. Whenever a magic attack came flying in, he’d stick that tail out like a lightning rod and protect everyone.”
Ah, I understood the feeling well. Having a magical lightning rod would be quite reassuring indeed.
“That boy’s descendants live in this world, you know. Thinking about that, sometimes I just want to check in on them. Isn’t it the same for you?”
“…Yeah, it is.”
So that was the reason Arc had originally stopped by this world in the first place. Something occurred to me, so I asked once more.
“How long ago was this, might I ask?”
“Hmm… he settled here around the time life first took root in this world, I’d imagine—back when there was still only a single Legendary Weapon. I came along much, much later than that.”
“Just how long ago is that supposed to be?!”

According to Father and the others’ research, each world was originally meant to have only one set of Legendary Weapons, yet the world we now stood in had eight. They’d merged together due to the chaos caused by the Crimson Swine’s true body. But apparently there’d been events even before all that. Arc really had been visiting this world for an extraordinarily long time. I turned my gaze to Ho-kun. Had he been coming here too, perhaps?
“This is my first time here. So please don’t look at me with those glittering, expectant eyes.”
Sparkle, sparkle. Ah, what a shame. If only Ho-kun had visited in the past, there’d have been more to investigate.

“Demon Lord Beast…” Big Sister murmured under her breath. Come to think of it, there had been that matter of trying to unlock a new weapon using Big Sister’s hair, which hadn’t worked out. Older Sister had once said something about the Raccoon-species being close by yet somehow distant…

“Demon lord, huh. Whether they called him that because he was some kind of cursed child or whatever, it’s a pretty ominous title. Well… I suppose anyone people find distasteful tends to get called a demon lord. Even in this world, we call the head of an enemy nation a demon lord.”
“Similar sort of thing, yeah~ In the terms you’d use from your Japan, I suppose they’d call it the king of demonic beings, hence demon lord.”
“Hero versus demon lord sounds like quite the contrast, but honestly, going by game logic, it’s really more like assassin versus king, isn’t it~?”

Ho-kun teased on. Admittedly, there was some truth to that. A hero is an individual, while a demon lord is a king, after all. In this world, heroes carried an aspect of being objects of worship—gods, in a sense, who solved all manner of problems.
